target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the Feishu channel pattern.
- On timeout, explicitly **destroy** the source (if it supports `destroy`) so the underlying Readable/HTTP resource closes, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting. Silence the losing `nextPromise` to avoid unhandledRejection.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled.
- Extract `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` as the production save chokepoint so loopback proofs drive the exact path Baileys streams enter.
- ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 asked for live WhatsApp timeout+recovery. This refresh supplies the strongest **local-server** proof at the Baileys Readable/HTTP boundary (timeout + destroy + server connection close + healthy progressing path), without live credentials. Live multi-message dispatch remains explicitly out of scope below.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "whatsapp chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Baileys media stream would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after 30s idle with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The source is destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `5c2efdffee2122d39c2b853af385fbca3eedf619`
- `oxfmt` on touched WhatsApp inbound media files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.idle.proof.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

- Mutation check: removing `destroySource(source)` makes HTTP loopback `destroyed=true` / `server_close=true` fail; restoring passes.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` before this proof refresh.

## Evidence

See **Real behavior proof** for exact `node --import tsx` transcript. Vitest includes the same HTTP `IncomingMessage` case.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled WhatsApp/Baileys-like media download stream, with source destroy + HTTP connection close.
Real environment tested: Node 22, production `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` / `saveMediaStream`, local `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` (headers flushed, body stalled), Node `IncomingMessage` Readable — same boundary Baileys stream downloads expose. No live WhatsApp session.
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/proof-whatsapp-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=5c2efdffee2122d39c2b853af385fbca3eedf619

[case 1] negative control — stalled HTTP body without idle wrap
  ok: stalled HTTP Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=302 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled HTTP body with idle wrap
  ok: timed out (not resolved)
  ok: error is WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError
  ok: timeout fires within 3s
  ok: timeout fires after the idle budget
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  ok: server observed client/connection close after destroy
  info: elapsed_ms=86 timed_out=true destroyed=true server_close=true chunkTimeoutMs=80

[case 3] valid response — progressing HTTP body
  ok: saved media size matches input
  ok: contentType preserved
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: stalled HTTP body without idle wrap stays pending (`outcome=still-pending`)
- Positive control: idle wrap rejects with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, `destroyed=true`, `server_close=true`
- Valid path: progressing HTTP JPEG saves (`size=4 timed_out=false`)
- Vitest HTTP case asserts the same destroy + server close contract

What was not tested: Live WhatsApp/Baileys cloud media download, real device session, or end-to-end subsequent-message dispatch after a live stall. Proof is controlled local-server at the Node Readable/HTTP boundary.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Wraps an existing AsyncIterable with a timeout raceguard. No new config/env. Progressing streams unchanged. Timeout destroys the source Readable so sockets do not accumulate after releasing the agent workflow. AI-assisted.
